belongs_to: Figure it Out Q1(b) (book p.180): 'Find the following products. Use a unit square as a whole for representing the fractions' - 1/4 x 1/3, printed answer 1/12
description: Unit-square area model for 1/4 x 1/3. Small label '(b)' printed at the top-left, outside the grid. The whole is drawn as a black-outlined grid of 4 equal columns by 3 equal rows = 12 equal cells (the whole is drawn as a square, about 221 x 220 px on the page, each cell a tall rectangle about 55 wide x 73 tall). The entire top row (all 4 cells) is filled light yellow = the 1/3 part of the whole. The top-left cell of that row is additionally covered with thin black diagonal hatch lines running from top-left down to bottom-right, on the yellow = the product (1/12). A curved black arrow starts at a label, left of and below the grid, that reads the stacked fractions 1/4 x 1/3 with a multiplication sign between them, and its arrowhead points at the hatched cell. To the right of the top row: a square bracket ']' spanning exactly the height of the top row, with the stacked fraction 1/3 printed to its right. Further right: a plain vertical line the full height of the grid, broken in the middle by the text '3 parts'. Below the grid: a plain horizontal line the full width of the grid, broken in the middle by the text '5 parts'. The other 8 cells (rows below the top row) are white. No other numbers, no ticks. Printed answer beside the figure (text, not part of the picture): Ans 1/12.
unclear: The text under the grid reads '5 parts' although the grid has only 4 columns (4 vertical cells across); treated as a misprint copied from figure (a) - the correct label would be '4 parts'. Decide whether to reproduce the misprint (not recommended) or print '4 parts'.
Number of hatch lines in the top-left cell not counted (about 6, not mathematical).

belongs_to: Figure it Out (book p.193): 'In each of the figures given below, find the fraction of the big square that the shaded region occupies' - Fig. (a); printed answer 3/8 of the area of the whole square
description: Fig. (a), the left of two squares printed side by side; the letter '(a)' is printed centred under it. Take the big square with corners TL, TR, BR, BL, centre O, side = 1 unit. All lines are black. (1) Both diagonals TL-BR and BL-TR are drawn in full and cross at O. (2) A vertical segment from the midpoint of the top side straight down to O, and a horizontal segment from O straight to the midpoint of the right side; together with the top side and right side they enclose the top-right quarter square (side 1/2). (3) Inside that top-right quarter square: a vertical segment through its centre (from the quarter's top side down to its bottom side, i.e. to the O-to-right-midpoint segment) and a horizontal segment through its centre (from the quarter's left side across to the right side of the big square), cutting the quarter into 4 equal small squares (each side 1/4); the diagonal BL-TR (O to TR) runs through the centre of the quarter and so through the common corner of the 4 small squares. (4) One more segment joins the midpoint of the left side to the midpoint of the bottom side (parallel to the diagonal TL-BR, at half the distance from BL); it crosses the half-diagonal BL-O at the centre of the bottom-left quarter. Shaded (11 orange-brown hatch lines drawn in the '/' direction, bottom-left to top-right, evenly spaced, 5 on each side of O plus one lying along the half-diagonal BL-O between the segment of (4) and O): the band between the diagonal TL-BR and the segment of (4) - a trapezoid with vertices left-side midpoint, TL, BR, bottom-side midpoint (it is the triangle under the diagonal, area 1/2, minus the corner triangle at BL, area 1/8). The top-right quarter, the triangle above/right of the diagonal and the corner triangle at BL are not shaded. No numbers or letters inside the figure.
unclear: The exact number of hatch lines (counted 11 by pixel analysis; one of them is partly hidden under the half-diagonal near O) does not matter mathematically.
The printed answer text says the shaded region of Fig. (a) is 3/8; this matches the band geometry described (1/2 - 1/8).

belongs_to: Figure it Out (book p.193): 'In each of the figures given below, find the fraction of the big square that the shaded region occupies' - Fig. (b); printed answer 1/16 of the area of the whole square ('the red shaded part')
description: Fig. (b), the right of two squares printed side by side; the letter '(b)' is printed centred under it. Big square, side = 1 unit, black outline. A horizontal line is drawn across the full width at mid height; a vertical line goes from the midpoint of the top side down to that horizontal line. So the square is cut into three regions: the top-left quarter square (side 1/2), the top-right quarter square (blank, 1/4 of the whole) and the whole bottom half (a 2:1 rectangle, blank, 1/2 of the whole). Inside the top-left quarter square a tilted square (diamond) is drawn whose 4 vertices are the midpoints of the quarter's 4 sides (top, right, bottom, left); the diamond is white and is half the area of the quarter. The four corner triangles of the quarter outside the diamond: the two on the left (top-left corner and bottom-left corner) are white; the two on the right - the corner triangle at the top-right of the quarter (between the diamond's upper-right edge, the quarter's top side and its right side) and the corner triangle at the bottom-right of the quarter (between the diamond's lower-right edge, the quarter's bottom side and its right side) - are filled with orange-brown hatch lines in the '/' direction: 4 lines in the upper triangle and 2 lines in the lower triangle (6 in all). Each corner triangle = 1/8 of the quarter, so the shaded part = 2 x 1/8 x 1/4 = 1/16 of the whole square. No numbers or letters inside the figure.
unclear: The printed answer calls the hatching 'red shaded'; on the page it is orange-brown.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q10 (book p.196-197): 'What fraction of the whole square is shaded?'; printed answer 3/32 of the whole square
description: Square, black outline, side = 1 unit, cut into 4 equal quarter squares by a vertical line and a horizontal line through the centre (full length each). The top-left, top-right and bottom-left quarters are completely blank. The bottom-right quarter (side 1/2, area 1/4 of the whole) has three more segments: from its top-left corner (= centre of the big square) a segment goes diagonally down-right, and from its top-right corner (= midpoint of the big square's right side) a segment goes diagonally down-left; they meet at a point at the centre of that quarter, forming a 'V' with a white triangle above it (apex down, 1/4 of the quarter); from that apex a vertical segment goes straight down to the bottom side of the big square. The quarter is thus cut into: the V-shaped top triangle (white), the left piece (quadrilateral with vertices: the quarter's top-left corner, the apex, the foot of the vertical segment on the bottom side, the quarter's bottom-left corner), and the right piece (mirror image, white). Only the left piece is shaded: 5 orange-brown hatch lines in the '/' direction. It is 3/8 of the quarter = 3/32 of the whole. No numbers or letters in the figure.
unclear: On the page the apex of the V sits just a little above the exact centre of the quarter; the printed answer 3/32 requires it exactly at the centre.
